source.title: When to Trust Your Model: Model-Based Policy Optimization.
source.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)

confidence_rationale: Provides the computational template the chip's confabulation caution demands: imagined (model-generated) trajectories are usable but only within a bounded, uncertainty-gated regime -- short rollouts branched from real data, horizon decoupled from task horizon and set by measured model generalization, with a monotonic-improvement guarantee. Structurally identical to MECH-322 (bounded/audited/provisional-until-corroborated). Confidence discounted: MBPO bounds VALUE error, not provenance/confabulation confusion -- the analogy is structural, not a validated transfer of the specific guard.
failure_signatures: Trusting imagined rollouts at long horizon lets the policy exploit regions where the learned model deviates from reality (model exploitation / compounding error); the REE analogue is retained-candidate content that, used unboundedly, drifts off the real manifold and self-reinforces.

Without an uncertainty-gated trust bound, model-generated data ceases to be preferable to real off-policy data -- i.e. unbounded retention/imagination use is not merely risky but provably worse than using less of it.

mapping.source_claim_statement: MBPO uses short model rollouts branched from real environment states to reduce compounding model error and decouple the model (imagination) horizon from the task horizon; a monotonic-improvement analysis shows real off-policy data is preferable to model-generated data unless an empirical estimate of model generalization justifies limited model usage, which then yields faster, higher-performing learning.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the computational form of the MECH-322 template the chip requires MECH-486 to follow. Retained rejected candidates (imagined, non-executed content) may feed evaluation/learning only under a bounded, uncertainty-gated, corroboration-limited regime: MBPO's short trust horizon gated by measured model error maps onto MECH-322's fail-closed conditions plus accelerated dissolution of any chunk not corroborated by real waking execution. It also gives a concrete knob: the trust bound should scale inversely with model uncertainty -- REE's epistemic_deficit (MECH-482) -- linking leg 3 retention to the same confidence term that gates the orient/survey leg of MECH-485.
mapping.mapping_caveat: MBPO bounds VALUE-estimation error for policy optimization; it does not address provenance confusion or the confabulation/reality-monitoring failure that is MECH-486's central hazard. The transfer is structural (bounded, provisional, corroboration-gated use of imagined content), not a validated import of the specific confabulation guard -- Schnider/Bouzerda-Wahlen supply that half, MBPO supplies the bounding discipline.
mapping.source_context: Deep model-based reinforcement learning; continuous-control MuJoCo benchmarks; learned probabilistic dynamics-model ensembles with short branched rollouts.

confidence_components.notes: Landmark, well-cited result with a formal bound. Mapping is a structural analogy to the MECH-322 template; transfer_risk high because MBPO's guarantee is about value error, not confabulation/provenance -- deliberately paired with the Schnider entries which cover the other half.
